## bench.customers
# `customers`
Columns: id, name, region_id, city, tier, credit, discount
Measures: _(none)_
Aggregations: _(none)_
Joins to: regions

SQL:
WITH _base AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS "orders.n"
  FROM orders AS orders
  LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
  WHERE
    NOT customers.id IS NULL
), _cm_orders__customers__credit_avg AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(AVG(customers.credit) AS DOUBLE) AS "customers.credit_avg"
  FROM customers AS customers
  WHERE
    NOT customers.id IS NULL
)
SELECT
  _cm_orders__customers__credit_avg."customers.credit_avg" AS "orders.avg_credit",
  _base."orders.n"
FROM _base
CROSS JOIN _cm_orders__customers__credit_avg
LIMIT 21

SQL:
WITH __slayer_stage_s1 AS (
  SELECT
    _stage_inner."orders.id" AS "id",
    _stage_inner."orders.customers.credit" AS "customers__credit"
  FROM (
    SELECT
      orders.id AS "orders.id",
      customers.credit AS "orders.customers.credit"
    FROM orders AS orders
    LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
      ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
    WHERE
      NOT customers.id IS NULL
    GROUP BY
      orders.id,
      customers.credit
  ) AS _stage_inner
)
SELECT
  CAST(AVG(s1.customers__credit) AS DOUBLE) AS "s1.avg_credit",
  COUNT(*) AS "s1.n"
FROM __slayer_stage_s1 AS s1
LIMIT 21

args.message:
The average credit limit is about 540.60 (540.5968063872256), with each order counted once. This covers the 5,010 orders that matched a customer.

I joined every order to its customer and averaged that customer's credit limit across all the orders, so a customer with many orders counts more. Orders with null credit values were left out of the average. If you instead average once per customer, you get 553.61. That is the per-customer figure, not the one you asked for.
